text:
Brad Marchand opened the season with a goal in Anaheim, played once more, then missed the rest of October and most of November injured. He returned with Aleksander Barkov on Wednesday against Ottawa and set up three goals in 14.2 minutes, as if he'd never left. Three games is nothing to judge, but the shape of it looks like him: 11 shots, 62% of the five-on-five shot attempts with him on the ice, and a heavy dose of carrying the puck into the zone.

The questions are the ones a 38-year-old with two Stanley Cups and 1,152 games behind him always faces. NHL EDGE puts his top skating speed in the bottom 1% of forwards this season, and Evolving-Hockey's 2025-26 numbers show the trade he makes: he drove offense (91st percentile for chances created) but opponents got more with him out there too (bottom 2%). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 8.9 primary shot assists per 60, 87th percentile. Watch his minutes: 12.3 a night is a soft landing, and our numbers project 43 points if he plays every game left.
headline: Marchand at 38: three games back, four points
